content.value:
Open CommandDecoratorsOpMode.java.

It declares a motor, gets it from hardwareMap, and has three examples in initialize().

Run the OpMode and look at Example 1 — a RunCommand with .withTimeout(3000) chained on. The motor runs at half power for 3 seconds and stops, even though RunCommand normally never finishes.

Example 2 shows asProxy() — it defers command creation until the command is actually scheduled. This is useful for button bindings where you want a fresh command instance each press.

Example 3 shows until() — it takes a BooleanSupplier and stops the command when the condition becomes true, checked every tick.

Remove the schedule() call from Example 1.

Write your own: a SequentialCommandGroup with an InstantCommand that sets power to 0.5, a WaitCommand with duration 5000, and an InstantCommand that sets power to 0.0.

Chain .withTimeout(2000) onto the SequentialCommandGroup. Schedule it.

The motor starts, runs for only 2 seconds (the timeout overrides the 5-second wait), then stops.

Remove the previous schedule() call.

Write a new one: a RunCommand that sets motor power to 0.3. Chain .withTimeout(3000) onto it. Schedule it.

The motor runs at 30% power for exactly 3 seconds and stops.

SolversLib also provides .beforeStarting(), .andThen(), .deadlineWith(), .alongWith(), .withInterrupt(), and .repeatedly().

Every one works on any command type.

Chain them together for exactly the behavior you need.
